Question: Given \(\dfrac{\log a}{p}=\dfrac{\log b}{q}=\dfrac{\log c}{r}=\log x,\) all logarithms to the same base and \(x\ne1.\) If \(\dfrac{b^2}{ac}=x^y,\) then \(y\) is:
Solution:
The displayed logarithms require \(a,b,c,x>0\), and the fractions require \(p,q,r\ne0\). The common logarithm base is positive and different from \(1\).

Multiplying each given equality by its denominator gives
\[
\log a=p\log x,\qquad
\log b=q\log x,\qquad
\log c=r\log x.
\]
Taking the logarithm of \(b^2/(ac)\) turns the products and powers into a linear combination:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\log\left(\frac{b^2}{ac}\right)
&=2\log b-\log a-\log c\\
&=(2q-p-r)\log x.
\end{aligned}
\]
But \(b^2/(ac)=x^y\), so the same logarithm is \(y\log x\). Consequently,
\[
y\log x=(2q-p-r)\log x.
\]
Since \(x\ne1\), we have \(\log x\ne0\), so division is valid. Thus
\[
\boxed{y=2q-p-r},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
